title: AI Peer Review per-repo config
description: Drop this file at .peer-review.json in a consuming repo's root (legacy location .github/ai-peer-review.json still works) to tailor classification, reviewer rosters, head-lock paths, ceilings, and escalation timing. Every field is optional; omitted fields use generic safe defaults. Unknown keys are ignored (forward compatible). Wrong types fail the run loudly so a bad config can never silently misclassify. NOTE: the format is JSON, not YAML — the dispatcher is stdlib-only and ships no YAML parser.

project_name.description: Human-readable project name used in comments/emails.

operator_github_login.description: GitHub login of the human operator who can issue OPERATOR commands and receives escalations.

project_description.description: One or two sentences about what this repo is, injected into every reviewer prompt (e.g. 'a paper-only trading system; it never places broker orders'). Tailors reviews to the tenant's domain. Default: empty (generic prompt).

review_guidance.description: Project-specific bug classes for reviewers to hunt for, injected into the prompt as a 'specifically for THIS project, also look for' list (e.g. lookahead bias, broker order paths). Default: empty (generic adversarial review only).

high_stakes_paths.description: fnmatch globs. Any changed file matching these forces the high_stakes tier (strictest review + escalation). Unknown paths already default to high_stakes (deny-first); list the files most dangerous to change.

content_scan_safety_tokens.description: Literal substrings; if any appears in the diff, the PR is high_stakes regardless of path.

content_scan_safety_patterns.description: Python regexes; if any matches the diff, the PR is high_stakes regardless of path.

routine_root_exact.description: Exact root-level filenames treated as routine (docs/config), e.g. README.md.

routine_root_globs.description: Root-level-only globs treated as routine, e.g. *.md (does NOT match nested markdown).

backend_path_roots.description: Path prefixes considered backend code (not safety-relevant), e.g. src/, tests/.

head_lock_paths.description: fnmatch globs (same syntax as high_stakes_paths). A high-stakes PR touching any of these requires explicit operator sign-off before merge even when all AI reviewers approve. Use for the most safety-critical files (e.g. broker/promotion/safety modules). Default: empty (tier rules alone).

routine_reviewers.description: Reviewer roster for the routine tier.

backend_reviewers.description: Reviewer roster for the backend tier.

high_stakes_reviewers.description: Reviewer roster for the high_stakes tier.

max_review_rounds.description: Hard cap on review rounds before forced escalation.

per_pr_cost_ceiling_usd.description: Per-PR spend ceiling; exceeding it escalates instead of spending more.

daily_cost_ceiling_usd.description: Rolling 24h spend ceiling across the repo.

escalation_cooldown_minutes.description: Minutes the dev agent must be quiet (no new commit) before a review-outcome escalation (reviewer dissent, CI persistently failing, head-lock touch, suspicious unanimity) pings the operator. A new commit resets the timer and silently re-runs review, so the phone never fires mid-iteration. Default 10. Set 0 to ping immediately (pre-Cut-1 behavior). Infra/budget escalations (cost ceiling, API outage) always ping immediately regardless.
